Hi Satoshi and Le —

Thanks for your interest in Redwood. We'd love to run a 30–45 minute demo focused on your inference workloads and how we can improve latency/cost for APAC traffic. To avoid the usual timezone mix-ups, here are a few overlapping windows we can offer next week (local times shown):

- Option A: 15:00 JST / 14:00 SGT / 16:00 AEST (Tue 2026-02-11)
- Option B: 11:00 JST / 10:00 SGT / 12:00 AEST (Wed 2026-02-12)
- Option C: 09:00 JST / 08:00 SGT / 10:00 AEST (Thu 2026-02-13)

Note: we (Redwood) are on PST and will automatically include UTC offsets in the invite, but let me know if any of these map to the wrong day on your calendars (I know next-day confusion happens when crossing the dateline).

Attached is a short agenda; we can tailor it to include a short Q&A and a brief look at cost estimates for your traffic pattern.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood-demo-agenda.pdf
From: Satoshi Tanaka <satoshi.tanaka@tokyo-retail.jp>

Date: 2026-02-10T16:15:00+09:00
Subject: Re: Demo: Redwood Inference — APAC scheduling (Tokyo/Singapore/Sydney)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — afternoon in Tokyo works best for our product and ops folks. A couple of quick notes: Japan does not observe daylight savings, but Singapore and Sydney have different DST rules (Sydney will be on AEDT later in the year). For next week those three slots look fine.

Option A (15:00 JST on Tue 2026-02-11) is ideal for us. Could you confirm what that will show as on the calendar invite for participants in PST and AEST? We've had cases where a 15:00 JST invite shows as "previous day" for the west coast, which confuses attendees.

Thanks,
Satoshi
Senior Engineer, Tokyo Retail Co.

Hi Satoshi —

Perfect — we'll tentatively hold Option A (Tue 2026-02-11 at 15:00 JST). I'll make the invite explicit ("Tue 2026-02-11 15:00 JST / 07:00 PST / 16:00 AEST") to avoid the previous-day ambiguity.

Laura, can you please create the calendar event with all timezones shown and include the agenda? Also adding a note about timezone/DST in the description.

Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Quick internal note —

- Use explicit TZ labels in the event title and description (e.g., JST/SGT/AEST/PST) and include UTC offsets to prevent calendar clients from shifting the date.
- For APAC customers I prefer to add the primary local time first (15:00 JST) then other times in parentheses.
- If we expect participants from multiple APAC cities (Tokyo + Sydney) add both city labels rather than just AEST.

I'll be on the demo from our engineering team — please set the reminder to 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer
